subject: Keep postponed forced movement upright after swordfight teardown
description: Nescafe Profile_001 Restart replay-009 advanced past task 131 and diverged at frame 505 for Soldier 229: Original installed TransitionWaitingUprightWalkingUpright while Rust translated the postponed Move|FORCE_SWORD_MOVEMENT to the logical WalkingWithSword token. The movement had been authored while the soldier was swordfighting, postponed behind QuitSwordfight, and instructed again only after the lowering animation left the actor Waiting. Original Actor::Instruct stamps that live Waiting action state before Human::DetermineMovementAnimation; the FORCE flag is not consulted during translation. Rust instead used FORCE as an action-state override and sword-translation input. Removing those invented roles selected Original's ordinary upright transition, then exposed a frame-506 1.5x speed and sword sprite mismatch because the execution path independently treated FORCE itself as sword-motion context. Original Human::Execute consults FORCE only inside an already-translated WalkingWithSword/RunningWithSword order, where it prevents an orphaned logical sword move from aborting after the opponent list becomes empty. Runtime sword routing now depends only on the actor's sword movement action state or an actual logical sword movement order; FORCE remains attached solely for that source-authored Execute guard. A focused regression recreates a forced upright move postponed until after sword lowering and verifies ordinary transition 5, the preserved Waiting stamp, retained FORCE flag, and non-sword runtime routing. cargo fmt, the focused robin_engine test, and git diff --check pass.
